entries.title: The ages: Wood, Stone, Iron, Diamond, Nether
q: how does my town reach the next age
how do i get to the stone age
what does the town need for the next age
entries.answer: A town comes up through five ages by itself. Wood: timber, food, the storehouse, a shelter, houses and a well. Stone: stone and coal, a wall, beds for nearly everyone, a smeltery and meeting hall. Iron: iron for the watch's armour and the smith, a workshop, watchtower and market. Diamond: twice the iron, a lighthouse and a chapel, mines down to the diamonds. Nether: obsidian made the player's way and a lit gateway.
steps: Press J: the journal says what the town is short of for its next age.
Help: deliver Wanted orders, do errands, or sell it what it lacks.
The evening a town comes into a new age, everybody turns out for fireworks.
tips: After the Nether Age a town raises great works forever, each a quarter dearer than the last.

entries.title: A town's rank: village, town, city, capital
q: how does my village become a city
entries.answer: Rank goes on past the ages. Village: the Stone Age and 12 folk. Town: the Iron Age and 30 folk. City: the Diamond Age, renown 20 (two great works, or a museum of rare finds) and 50 folk. Capital: the Nether Age, renown 60, 80 folk and two colonies of its own. Renown is ten for every great work plus what its museum shows.

entries.title: How a town grows
q: how do i get more villagers
entries.answer: Two fed folk in work raise a child while there's room (a free bed) and the stores hold a day's meals for everybody. So the town builds a house whenever it's nearly full and farms ahead of its mouths: food put by, children, hands, materials, houses, room. Newcomers and refugees from other towns join too.
tips: A thriving town has children more readily (only three fifths of the usual larder needed).
A Village Folk Spawner placed in a town adds one settler.
warn: The server's growth cap (and the world's cap) stop children past a size.

entries.title: Newcomers, migration and refugees
q: why did a new villager arrive
entries.answer: Folk move: a town short a hand at a trade posts a Wanted notice, and a folk with a reason (out of work, unhappy) may apply and move there. Raids leave refugees who look for a new home. A folk thinking of leaving can be talked round: the talk screen offers 'Won't you stay?'.
controls: [Right-click] a folk thinking of leaving → Won't you stay?

entries.title: The town's mine
q: how does the village mine work
do folk dig under my town
entries.answer: A town digs one mine, away from its ground: a shaft with levels, drifts and branches, dug for what the town is short of (stone and coal, then iron at the iron seam, diamonds near the bottom for the Diamond Age). The mine's ground widens as levels are worked out, never under the town.
tips: Pit props hold up loose roofs; rope coils let miners down shafts; ore sacks carry more.
The Production page shows the mine's books.

entries.title: The cave team
q: what have the cave dwellers found
can i join the cave team
entries.answer: An Iron Age town of 25+ sends a small, skilled cave team (half miners, half guards, lamps on their helmets) into the caves round it for ore and rare finds. Ask any folk 'Their finds' (World → Underground); ask a cave dweller to look somewhere ('Cave team, look east'), take you along, or sell a copy of the cave map.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → World → Underground → Their finds
Cave dweller → World → Underground → Ask the delvers… · Go caving · Cave map

entries.title: The Nether runners
q: do folk go to the nether
can i go to the nether with villagers
what's it like in the nether
entries.answer: A Nether Age town lights its obsidian gateway and sends a picked team of Nether runners through to bring back what it can't get otherwise: nether wart, blaze rods, quartz, glowstone, ender pearls. Ask 'Their report' (World → The Nether); ask the runners for something ('Runners, bring us blaze rods'), to take you through, or for a copy of their chart.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → World → The Nether → Their report
A runner → Ask the runners… · Go through · Runners' chart
tips: Runners wear a Gold Charm (piglins leave them be) and carry a fire-proof Runner's Satchel.

entries.title: Research and inventions
entries.answer: A town studies civics (the Research page) and works out inventions (the Inventions page): twenty-two machines, buildings and arms in four branches (Agriculture, Engineering, Military, Learning), each waiting for its age. Its scholars work at their desks of an evening; each finished invention's working model goes into the stores and the museum.
steps: Open the town's books → Civic → Inventions.
Give, pick, sponsor or suggest from its buttons; the leader weighs a player's suggestion.

entries.title: The Village Storehouse
q: where does the village keep its items
how do i open the storehouse
entries.answer: The whole town keeps its goods in one Village Storehouse: 27 storehouse units stacked 3×3×3 join into a store that starts at 729 slots and never fills. Right-click any face: six rows at a time, a scroll bar, Sort, and a count of how full it is. You can build one of your own the same way.
steps: Craft 27 Storehouse Units (four planks and four sticks each).
Stack them in a 3×3×3 cube; the door is the middle of the bottom row facing you.
warn: Taking from a town's storehouse is theft unless you're a citizen. Break the door unit and the unit you pick up carries the goods.

entries.title: Where everything comes from (supply chains)
q: why is the town short of something
entries.answer: Nothing is conjured: every block, tool and meal has a way to it from what the land gives, through the town's own trades. Producers fill a production chest on their plot; couriers carry it to the storehouse; makers draw their makings; builders lay only what the stores hold. A missing link means a wait (or a Wanted order).
controls: Town's books → Economy → Production · Stores · Stock

entries.title: Borders and the town's lands
q: how far does my town reach
entries.answer: Each town has lands round it with borders against its neighbours; contested ground is disputed. The Lands page (Civic) shows their extent, the neighbours along the border, disputes and markers; the war room's map table draws them.

entries.title: Transport: roads, rails, ferries, harbours
q: how do i call the ferry
entries.answer: Towns build roads (with inns and milestones), railways, carts and wagons, ferries across water (ring the Ferry Bell at a landing to call the boat, or ask the ferryman 'Take me across'), bridges, and harbours with ships and a fishing fleet. The Transport, Roads and Harbour pages show them.
controls: Ferryman → Trade → Services → Take me across

entries.title: Does my town keep going when I'm away?
q: does my village work when im not there
does the town grow without me
what happens when i leave the village
entries.answer: Yes. A town keeps its own ground loaded and goes on with nobody near, for hundreds of days: working, building, growing, holding elections. When you come back, the nearest folk who knows you tells you what happened.
